co_lover_s_leap.blurb: Lover's Leap is a tall roadside cliff southwest of Denver, in the foothills above US 285 near Morrison and Evergreen, with gneiss walls. It is a traditional crag built around cracks, with a few bolted sections, and the face is big enough to allow many variations and multi-pitch outings of up to four pitches. The grades range from the 5.6 to 5.7 classics up to several 5.12 lines, though the bulk sit around 5.9 and 5.10. The walk to the base is steeper than the road view suggests, crossing a creek and winding up through talus. Rappelling is the usual way down. It suits climbers comfortable placing their own gear.

co_little_black_cliff.blurb: Little Black Cliff is a small crag at Big Meadows, up on Wolf Creek Pass in Colorado's San Luis Valley country, at roughly 8,700 feet. It is the gentlest of the three Big Meadows areas: a short, casual stroll from the road, and no avalanche exposure. Most of the sixteen routes are bolted sport lines of around six clips, with a handful of gear climbs and a mixed line or two. Grades start in the low 5.x range and run through the 5.7 to 5.9 zone to a few 5.11s. Most routes can also be toproped by walking around the side of the main cliff, which makes it handy for a short, low-key day.

co_fourth_buttress.blurb: Fourth Buttress is the last of the blocky Elephant Buttresses towers in Boulder Canyon, just west of Boulder, with a northwest face and a south face. Nearly everything here is traditional climbing, with an aid line and a few top-rope options, and bolts are scarce, so bring a full rack. Grades run from an easy fourth-class scramble through 5.7 to 5.9, with a solid cluster of 5.10 routes and one 5.11. The Northwest Face at 5.8 is the standout. Approach by crossing the bridge and following the climbers' trail up to the water pipe, which leads to the base. Poison ivy is plentiful and some rock is loose.

co_canyon_road_cliffs.blurb: Canyon Road Cliffs is a band of short cliffs in Witches' Canyon, a little southwest of Penitente Canyon in the San Luis Valley. Routes are about 30 to 50 feet tall and mostly bolted, with a few gear lines and a single hard boulder problem. Most of them catch good sun, and you can usually park close to the base, so there is little or no hiking. The grades span an easy 5.5 up through the 5.9 and 5.10 range, which is where most of the climbing sits, with a couple of 5.11s. It makes a relaxed stop for a quick session of short sport pitches.

co_needle_the_2.blurb: The Needle is a compact granite crag on the slope of Prospect Mountain above Estes Park, with open views over town. Climbs are short, one pitch for the most part and two at the very longest. Most of the sixteen routes are bolted sport lines, with some gear routes and a couple of top-ropes. Grades run from a beginner-level 5.0 slab to 5.13, with most between 5.8 and 5.11, so it works for a wide mix of abilities. Many of the sport routes were re-equipped with new lower-off anchors in 2022. It suits a quick session, a short day or marginal weather rather than a long outing.
co_needle_the_2.approach: From the signed trailhead on Peak View Drive, a trail of about three quarters of a mile climbs roughly 400 feet to the crag, usually taking 20 to 30 minutes.
